themes.label: Literature CARR builds on and the gap it fills
themes.need: A researcher deciding how to model volatility wants to know how CARR relates to and improves upon stochastic-volatility, range-based, and ARCH/GARCH modeling traditions, and what literature gap it fills.

themes.label: CARR model specification & exponential likelihood
themes.need: A researcher wants the formal specification of the CARR(p,q) dynamic range model and its log-likelihood under an exponential error assumption.

themes.label: CARR estimation properties: QMLE, GARCH equivalence, Weibull
themes.need: A researcher implementing CARR wants to know how to estimate it consistently via QMLE (including the GARCH-equivalence estimation trick), obtain robust standard errors, and generalize to a Weibull error distribution for efficiency.

themes.label: S&P500 range/return data & descriptive statistics
themes.need: A researcher wants descriptive statistics (kurtosis, ACF, Ljung-Box Q) of the S&P500 weekly return/range series used to motivate and validate the CARR model.
themes.distributed_justification: Table 1's descriptive numbers (kurtosis, Q-statistics) resume after the intervening model-variant/diagnostic-test description (assigned to the ECARR-results theme); both spans describe the same data.

themes.label: ECARR/ECARRX estimation results
themes.need: A researcher wants the estimated ECARR/ECARRX coefficients, diagnostics, and leverage-effect significance for weekly S&P500 range data under the exponential-error specification.
themes.distributed_justification: Table 1 (own theme, descriptive statistics) is interposed between the model-variant/diagnostic setup and the coefficient results/interpretation; both spans continue one ECARR-results argument.

themes.label: WCARR (Weibull) results vs exponential fit
themes.need: A researcher wants to know whether a Weibull error distribution improves on the exponential CARR specification, and the resulting WCARR/WCARRX coefficient estimates.
themes.distributed_justification: Figure 2/3 captions (trash, 274-278) interrupt the continuous Weibull-fit-quality discussion; both spans serve one need.

themes.label: Out-of-sample RMSE/MAE forecast comparison
themes.need: A researcher wants to compare CARR and GARCH out-of-sample volatility forecast accuracy (RMSE/MAE) across multiple realized-volatility proxies and horizons.

themes.label: Mincer-Zarnowitz single-regressor predictive power
themes.need: A researcher wants to test each model's forecasts individually via Mincer-Zarnowitz regressions to gauge which of CARR or GARCH has more predictive power for realized volatility.
themes.distributed_justification: The forecast-encompassing regression setup (eq. 11, own theme) is textually interposed between the Mincer-Zarnowitz regression discussion and Table 5 itself; both spans serve the single-regressor predictive-power need.

themes.label: Forecast-encompassing regression: methodology & results
themes.need: A researcher wants to know, via a forecast-encompassing regression, whether CARR's volatility forecast subsumes the information in GARCH's forecast (or vice versa).
themes.distributed_justification: The encompassing regression (eq. 11) is defined before Table 5 (Mincer-Zarnowitz results, own theme) is presented; its results (Table 6) and interpretation only follow after that intervening material.

themes.label: Conclusion: performance summary & future extensions
themes.need: A researcher scoping follow-up work on CARR wants to know what generalizations (multivariate, robust range measures, time-varying drift, diffusion, risk-premium tests, VaR) are proposed as future extensions.
themes.distributed_justification: Figure 4 caption (trash, 459-460) interrupts the single continuous conclusion/future-research paragraph.
